vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: extract-memories
Version: 2.0.2

The 'extract-memories' skill is a utility designed to help an AI agent summarize and persist conversation context into a structured local memory system (memory/topics/ and MEMORY.md). The instructions in SKILL.md define clear schemas for different memory types and include explicit constraints on what should not be saved (e.g., code structures, git history, or temporary states), which aligns with efficient and safe agent behavior. No indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or unauthorized access were found.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (extracting and persisting distilled conversation 'memories' into memory/topics/ and an index) matches its instructions and required permissions; the main user-facing risk is that it will persist conversation content to disk (possible sensitive data) and can optionally spawn child agents.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the SKILL.md instructions: it analyzes recent dialogue and writes topic files under memory/topics/ and updates MEMORY.md. The requested capabilities (reading dialogue context and writing files) are what this feature legitimately needs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly scoped to recent conversation lines and to creating/updating topic files and an index. The skill explicitly forbids saving code structure, Git history, temp status, etc. Note: because it persists extracted content to disk automatically at conversation end (and exposes a manual /extract-memories trigger), there is a privacy risk — sensitive PII or secrets could be saved unless the agent or user filters them. The SKILL.md does state heuristics (ask before saving certain types), but it does not mandate explicit user confirmation for each saved item.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec, no downloads, and no code files — lowest install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, binaries, or external credentials are requested. The declared permissions (FileRead, FileWrite/FileEdit on memory files, optional sessions_spawn) are proportionate to the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (good). The skill is intended to run automatically at conversation end (autonomous invocation allowed by default on the platform), which coheres with its behavior. Consider that automatic persistence of conversation content increases the attack/ privacy surface — combined with optional sessions_spawn (forking a child agent) this raises operational considerations even if not intrinsically malicious.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and implements what it claims: it will extract items from recent chat turns and append them as topic files under memory/topics/ and add pointers to MEMORY.md. Before installing, consider: 1) where the memory/ directory will live and who can read those files (ensure file-system permissions and backups are acceptable); 2) whether you want automatic, end-of-dialog persistence — if you prefer manual control, avoid auto-invocation or disable/limit the skill; 3) sensitive data risk — the skill may accidentally persist PII/secrets unless you configure the agent to filter or require confirmation before saving; 4) the optional sessions_spawn capability (child agent forks) may be unnecessary for your use case — only grant it if you understand the behavior. If you want stronger guarantees, ask the skill author for an explicit opt-in prompt before each write, or audit the memory/ files regularly and limit their retention.
